Screen a panel of external models against a target

screenExternals.Rd

Runs the screening cascade: remove degenerate models, apply exactly one screen, rank the survivors, de-duplicate them in rank order and optionally keep the best K.

Usage

screenExternals(
  beta.external,
  fit = NULL,
  X.val = NULL,
  y.val = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  corr = NULL,
  XtX = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  bar = 1,
  nfolds = 3L,
  seed = NULL,
  dedup.cor = 0.9,
  top.k = NULL,
  degenerate.tol = 1e-08,
  labels = NULL,
  trace = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'BRIER.screen'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

beta.external

A p x M matrix of external coefficients, no intercept row. A (p+1) x M matrix with an intercept row is accepted and the row is dropped.

fit

A BRIER fit of the target at eta = 0, supplying the coefficient path the folds re-select on. Required by the CV screen.

X.val, y.val

The validation split, on the RAW scale. Standardisation moments are taken from each fold's training folds and applied to the held-out fold, so a pre-standardised split would let the held-out samples set their own scale.

covariates

An optional n x q matrix or data frame of covariates to residualise y.val against. For a gaussian outcome, y.val is residualised on these (when given) and then STANDARDISED, both refitted SEPARATELY within each piece of each fold so neither piece sees the other. The result does not depend on the scale y.val is supplied on. Binary and count outcomes are used as given.

corr

A length-p vector of the target's marginal correlations. Required by the validation-free screen.

XtX

A p x p LD matrix, sparse or dense. Required by the validation-free screen.

n

The target's GWAS sample size, setting the no-signal floor. Required by the validation-free screen.

family

One of "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson".

bar

The relative bar for the CV screen, applied to both legs. Defaults to 1, meaning the external must match the target-only model.

nfolds

Number of cross-validation folds. Defaults to 3.

seed

Seed for the fold assignment. NULL leaves the RNG alone.

dedup.cor

Absolute cosine similarity at which a survivor counts as a duplicate of one already kept. NULL or NA disables the step.

top.k

Keep only the best K survivors after de-duplication. NULL keeps them all.

degenerate.tol

A model whose coefficients are all zero, or whose PRS variance falls below this, carries no signal and is removed before any screen runs.

labels

Optional names for the M external models.

trace

Logical. If TRUE, reports each fold as it runs.

x

A BRIER.screen object.

...

Ignored.

Value

A list of class "BRIER.screen":

externals

A data frame with one row per external model: its index and label, its nonzero count, whether it was degenerate, the screen's own statistics, keep (passed the screen), dedup (survived de-duplication and the top-K cut) and rank (position among the final set, 1 is best, NA for a model that did not reach it).

screen

Which screen ran, "cv" or "validation-free".

survivors

Indices passing the screen, before de-duplication.

kept

Indices of the final set, IN RANK ORDER.

rank.statistic

The column kept was ordered on.

n.degenerate,n.screened.out,n.deduplicated

What each stage removed.

bar,nfolds,floor

The settings the screen actually used.

Details

Which screen runs is decided by what is supplied, and the two are mutually exclusive. Supplying fit, X.val and y.val selects the CROSS-VALIDATED screen; supplying corr, XtX and n selects the VALIDATION-FREE screen. Supplying both is an error rather than a silent precedence rule, because the two answer different questions and a caller who supplies both has not decided which one they want.

The cross-validated screen

Each external model is judged RELATIVE to the target-only model on the same held-out samples, rather than against the null. The validation split is cut into nfolds folds; in each fold the two remaining folds choose lambda for the target-only path and fit the external's free intercept, and everything is scored on the held-out fold. No refitting happens: the coefficient path comes from fit, and the folds only re-select on it.

Both legs must pass, and each relative bar is CLIPPED BY THE NULL MODEL:

$$\mathrm{loss}_{ext} \le \min(\mathrm{bar}^{-1}\,\mathrm{loss}_{target},\ \mathrm{loss}_{null})$$ $$\mathrm{acc}_{ext} \ge \max(\mathrm{bar}\,\mathrm{acc}_{target},\ \mathrm{acc}_{floor})$$

The clips are load bearing in both directions. Without the loss cap the bar goes slack exactly when the target is weak, so a target at MSPE 1.0 would admit scores predicting worse than the mean. Without the accuracy floor the bar falls below chance whenever bar < 1, since the expected R-squared of a signal-free predictor is \(1/n\). Reported as the two ratios ratio_loss and ratio_acc, both oriented so that a value at or above 1 means the external beat its reference, and both averaged over folds PAIRED WITHIN FOLD so that fold difficulty cancels.

The accuracy floor uses the FOLD's n, not the split's. Each metric is measured on roughly 1/nfolds of the samples, and averaging folds cuts the variance of the estimate but not its null bias, so the floor stays where the measurement happened.

For a binary outcome the external's intercept follows the target's. Against a BRIERs fit, which has no intercept, the external gets none and the null is \(p = 0.5\). Against a BRIERi fit, which has one, the external's intercept is fitted off-fold, glm(y ~ 1, offset = score), and the null is the training folds' prevalence.

The validation-free screen

Computed from the coefficient vector, the target's marginal correlations and the LD alone, so it needs no held-out samples and cannot leak any. With \(b\) the external coefficients, \(r\) the marginal correlations and \(R\) the LD, both legs must pass:

$$d^2 = 2 b'r - b'Rb > 0 \qquad\text{and}\qquad R^2 = (b'r)^2 / (b'Rb) > \mathrm{floor}$$

\(d^2\) is \(1 - \mathrm{MSPE}\) for a standardised outcome, so the first leg asks that the score beat the mean at its published scale. The second is the squared correlation the score would achieve after the best rescaling, so it is scale free, and its floor is the no-signal level \(1/n\), with n the GWAS sample size of the target. The floor is \(1/n\) for EVERY family, binary outcomes included: \(R^2\) here is a squared correlation on the correlation scale BRIERs works in, not an AUC, so the 0.5 floor that belongs to an AUC does not apply to it.

See also

dedupExternals, BRIERi, BRIERs

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# validation-free: summary statistics and LD only
scr <- screenExternals(beta.external = B, corr = r, XtX = R, n = 150000,
                       family = "gaussian", top.k = 10)
scr$externals[scr$externals$dedup, ]

# cross-validated against a target-only fit
base <- BRIERs(sumstats, XtX, beta.external = B, eta.list = 0)
scr <- screenExternals(beta.external = B, fit = base,
                       X.val = X.val, y.val = y.val, family = "gaussian")
} # }
